title: Adaptive eviction policy and contextual page enrichment for SLO-driven paging
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our current paging surface generates high-volume low-signal pages during transient overloads and multi-region failovers. This exhausts on-call capacity and delays response to true SLO violations. Goals: 1) Reduce noisy pages by evicting low-signal alerts using SLO-aware heuristics and circuit-breaker state. 2) Enrich the pages we do send with contextual evidence so responders can take faster, safer action. 3) Automate low-risk mitigations (load-shedding, scaled rollbacks, model fallback) while ensuring human-in-the-loop for high-risk actions. Scope: alert de-duplication and eviction policy, page enrichment service (alert-enricher), runbook automation hooks, adjustments to multi-region failover thresholds, and new observability dashboards for verification.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume reduced by >=40% for non-customer-facing transient SLO degradations in the first week of canary
Pages include top-3 probable causes, last deploy id, recent canary results, circuit-breaker state, and suggested next-step runbook links
Automated mitigation executes in staging for low-risk conditions and requires manual confirmation for high-risk conditions
No regression in end-to-end customer-facing SLOs (error-rate P95) during rollout
Runbook executions are logged and auditable with a UUID attached to the alert
implementation_steps: Design eviction heuristic: combine SLO burn rate, source dedupe score, recent probe canary failures, and CB (circuit-breaker) state to compute a page score
Build alert-enricher service that queries SLO catalog, trace sampler, recent deploys, and CB telemetry; returns enriched payload for paging backend
Add policy layer to paging orchestrator to drop or suppress pages below a dynamic threshold and escalate to Slack-only notifications instead
Expose explicit 'evict-reason' tags on suppressed alerts for postmortem analysis
Integrate runbook hooks: low-risk mitigation playbooks (eg. traffic-steering, KV-cache eviction, graceful shedding) that can be auto-invoked with safety gates
Create canary in staging: route 10% of region B traffic through new orchestration for 72h and monitor false-negative rate
Dashboarding and SLO verification: add per-route page-rate, suppressed-page-reason, and mean-time-to-action metrics
Security review and audit logging for automated actions (KMS access if needed)
decisions: Use burn-rate over a 5m and 30m window for initial eviction scoring to balance quick detection and transient smoothing
Pages suppressed will be sent to a low-attention Slack channel with a single ephemeral badge; only pages above threshold will trigger phone/SMS pagers
Automated mitigations permitted only when at least two independent signals agree (SLO burn + circuit-breaker open + recent deploy absent)
Keep manual escalation path intact for any alert that affects customer-facing error-rate or latency SLOs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-suppression leading to missed incidents. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, staging canary, and audit sampling where 1 in 10 suppressed alerts still create a shadow page to measure false-negatives
Risk: Enrichment latency adds to alert pipeline. Mitigation: asynchronous enrichment with cached metadata and a 200ms budget; fallback to minimal payload if enrichment times out
Risk: Automated actions cause cascading failure. Mitigation: implement circuit-breaker pattern for automations and require explicit two-factor confirmation for rollbacks and on-prem actions

runbook_preview: If top-level route error-rate breaches 3x SLO in 5m and circuit-breaker is open: 1) Enrich alert (automated) -> gather trace id, deploy id, canary health, top spans. 2) If enrichment indicates recent deploy within 30m, page on-call & post deploy diff link. 3) If no recent deploy and burn-rate spike with CB open, trigger staging-only traffic steer (automated) and notify on-call. 4) If customer-facing SLO affected, escalate immediately to primary pager and execute rollback checklist (manual confirmation required).
